answer: Reputation-Weighted Thread Anchoring. Each identity's actions enter a shared thread keyed to its sponsor; a clone inherits its sponsor's visible history, so any echo of duplicate behavior is scored against that sponsor. New identities start with a cold anchor and cannot borrow trust. To launch N clones, an attacker must build N independent anchor histories, each requiring real sustained activity and exposure to the ocean of public audit. Marginal cost per clone exceeds expected gain from any single vote or task.
